story: Alex fidgeted with the frayed threads on his sleeve while waiting in the crowded waiting room. The hum of the fluorescent lights overhead felt too loud, and the smell of antiseptic made his stomach twist. He checked his watch for the third time in five minutes, each second stretching longer than the last. A nurse called his name, but he didn’t move at first, his breath catching as if the air had gone still around him. He forced himself to stand, hands trembling slightly as he reached for his crumpled folder of papers.

Alex stared at the clock, its ticking echoing louder with each passing second. His fingers drummed a restless rhythm on the table, the coffee in front of him long cold. He kept adjusting his posture, shifting from one leg to the other, as if searching for a position that might still his thoughts. The room felt smaller than it was, the air thick with silence. When the door finally creaked open, he jumped slightly, then forced a smile he wasn’t sure reached his eyes.

Alex checked his phone for the third time in five minutes, though he knew there was nothing new to see. His fingers tapped an uneven rhythm against the table, each tap louder than the last. The coffee in front of him had gone cold, forgotten beside a half-eaten muffin. He kept glancing at the clock, willing time to move faster, though every second felt stretched and heavy. When the door opened, he started, his breath catching in his throat.
